newsitem.title: INDIA: Camdessus welcomes moves on rupee convertibility.
newsitem.headline: Camdessus welcomes moves on rupee convertibility.

text.p: International Monetary Fund (IMF) managing director Michel Camdessus on Wednesday welcomed India's decision to set up a panel to chart the path towards rupee capital account convertibility, a government statement said.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram last week in the 1997/98 (April-March) federal budget asked the Reserve Bank of India to set up a panel to "lay out the road map towards capital account convertibility."
"Mr Camdessus welcomed the announcement of a committee to chart the course towards capital account convertibility," the government statement said.
The rupee was made convertible on the current account transactions of the balance of payments in August 1994. Current account refers to transactions in goods and services.
Capital account convertibility implies the freedom to transact in financial assets with foreign countries without any restrictions.
